description: What flush and shutdown report (REQ-DLV-010). The core is built with the given destinations (each one a log sink with the behavior given: ok answers Accepted for the whole batch after delay_ms, hang never answers, fail answers Failed for the whole batch, drop answers Dropped for the whole batch), with batch_size and flush_interval_ms as given, then events log events are emitted, then flush or shutdown is called with timeout_ms. Counting: each destination has its own queue, so one event for two destinations is two deliveries; sent is the number of events a destination accepted, dropped is every other event that was queued (or being sent) when the call began and was not accepted by the end: dropped or failed by the destination, or still queued or in flight at the timeout (their outcome is not known); spooled is always 0 until the spool exists (T-06). A flush sends the partial batches at once (it does not wait for the flush interval). returns_before_timeout says whether the call may return before timeout_ms (true) or only at the timeout (false); a test checks that a call with true returns in less than timeout_ms, and a call with false in at least 80% of timeout_ms and in at most timeout_ms plus a margin. The shape of the expected values is the same for flush and shutdown.

cases.name: healthy_destination
cases.description: A healthy destination: every queued event is sent at once, although the flush interval is 60 s and the batch is not full, and the call returns before its timeout.

cases.name: two_healthy_destinations
cases.description: Each destination has its own queue: 3 events are 6 deliveries.

cases.name: nothing_queued
cases.description: Nothing queued: the result is zero and the call returns at once.

cases.name: a_hanging_destination
cases.description: A destination that never answers: the call returns at its timeout, the 4 events of that destination are dropped, and the healthy destination sent its 4.

cases.name: a_failing_destination
cases.description: A destination that answers Failed for every event: those events are lost and counted as dropped (there is no retry yet).

cases.name: a_dropping_destination
cases.description: A destination that answers Dropped for every event.

cases.name: a_slow_destination_that_finishes
cases.description: Each send takes 100 ms and the batch is 2: 6 events take 300 ms, inside the timeout of 1500 ms.

cases.name: a_slow_destination_that_does_not_finish
cases.description: Each send takes 500 ms and the batch is 2: at the timeout of 750 ms one batch was sent (2) and the other 4 events are dropped (the second send is still running).
